title: [Bugs] AMF fails to decode Registration Request(GUTI) after restart
pass1_rationale: After AMF restart the lost NAS security context makes the AMF fail to decode GUTI registration instead of falling back.
pass2_rationale: After an AMF restart it has lost the UE's NAS security context. The AMF then fails to decode the ciphered inner Registration Request (GUTI), and registration stops instead of falling back to authentication. The UE cannot re-register and the AMF logs a decode error.

title: [Bugs] The UE will not reconnect if the AMF reboots without sending a deregistration to the UE.
pass1_rationale: A restarted AMF forgets UEs and silently drops their Service Requests; UEs never re-register.
pass2_rationale: After an AMF reboot all UE contexts are lost. The AMF silently drops Service Requests from UEs that still think they are registered, instead of sending Service Reject #9, so the UEs retry forever and never reconnect. The AMF logs a state-mismatch error.

title: [Bugs] UPF leaks PfcpXact if PFCP Session Report Response is not processed
pass1_rationale: UPF leaks a PFCP transaction if the Session Report Response is never processed; peer failure plausible but not shown.
pass2_rationale: When SMF is unreachable (Session Report Responses dropped via iptables), UPF never frees the PfcpXact for PFCP Session Report, leaking transactions until pfcpXactPool is empty; afterwards new PFCP procedures (Service Request modification) keep failing. Leak itself raises no error until exhaustion; the reproducer exhausts it within one test.

title: [Bugs] N3IWUE reconnection causes communicateWithUDM error: SYSTEM_FAILURE at AMF.
pass1_rationale: N3IWUE reconnection yields SYSTEM_FAILURE at AMF; root cause unclear.
pass2_rationale: N3IWUE reconnect after Ctrl+C fails with communicateWithUDM SYSTEM_FAILURE until UDM is restarted; the triggering event is a UE (N3IWUE) restart, not an NF/peer failure (UE-only event per codebook), and no root cause in thread.

title: [Bugs] SMF reports "IP is used" and "UE IP pool exhausted" after gNB CU/DU restart
pass1_rationale: After gNB CU/DU restart the SMF retains the UE's old IP allocation; 'IP is used' and eventually 'UE IP pool exhausted'.
pass2_rationale: After killing and restarting gNB CU/DU (SCTP shutdown, new NGSetup), SMF's previously allocated UE IP is not released, so SMF reports 'IP is used' / 'UE IP pool exhausted' and PDU session establishment is not accepted until free5GC is restarted. Intermittent but persistent once hit.

title: [Bugs] SMF Resource Exhaustion via PFCP Session Establishment Failure Handling
pass1_rationale: When the UPF does not answer Session Establishment, resources allocated for the failed attempt are never released.
pass2_rationale: When UPF PFCP Session Establishment Responses are dropped (UPF unreachable on N4), SMF never releases the SM context/UE IP after PFCP timeout, so repeated failures exhaust the IP pool; thread: fix releases SM context on the reject path. Failure is logged/visible per attempt and exhaustion needs many cycles (pool shrunk to /29).

title: [Bugs] SMContext leaked when GetTokenCtx fails during SM context create; empty 200 leaves the AMF with no smContextRef to release it
pass1_rationale: During an NRF outage every SM context create leaks an SMContext the AMF has no smContextRef to release.
pass2_rationale: During an NRF outage, GetTokenCtx fails in SM context create and SMF returns an empty 200 without releasing the SMContext (UE IP, TEIDs), so each request leaves an SMContext the AMF has no ref to release. 'Get Token Context Error' is logged; the leak grows with no ceiling but stays internal state in a short test.

title: [Bugs] SMContext leaked when GetTokenCtx fails during SM context create; empty 200 leaves the AMF with no smContextRef to release it
pass1_rationale: During an NRF outage every SM context create leaks an SMContext the AMF has no smContextRef to release.
pass2_rationale: During an NRF outage, GetTokenCtx fails in SM context create and SMF returns an empty 200 without releasing the SMContext (UE IP, TEIDs), so each request leaves an SMContext the AMF has no ref to release. 'Get Token Context Error' is logged; the leak grows with no ceiling but stays internal state in a short test.

title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
pass1_rationale: PFCP setup failure after 201 Created leaks SMContext/IP/TEIDs; trigger need not be a peer failure.
pass2_rationale: When PFCP establishment fails (UPF associated but unresponsive) and/or the AMF is unreachable for N1N2MessageTransfer after the 201, SMF early-returns without RemoveSMContext, leaking SMContexts, UE IPs and TEIDs (31 requests leak 31); only WARN logs about the failed transfer, slow leak not visible to a short test. Thread: reject side already fixed in #236, accept side still open.

title: [Bugs] SM policy leaked on every failure path after NewUeSmPolicyData; error response omits Location so the SMF can never delete it
pass1_rationale: SM policy leaked on PCF failure paths; failures need not come from a peer outage.
pass2_rationale: During an NRF outage (oauth GetTokenCtx fails) PCF CreateSmPolicy fails after the policy entry is inserted. It returns an error without Location, so the SMF can never delete the SM policy: an orphan entry, bounded at about 15 per UE and overwritten on reuse. The create failure is visible at that time (HTTP 500), so not silent; the effect is internal state only.

title: [Bugs] UPF PFCP Association Setup overwrite
pass1_rationale: Association overwrite on re-setup loses forwarding state; framed as an authentication flaw.
pass2_rationale: Security report: an unauthorized peer sends a PFCP Association Setup claiming an existing SMF Node ID and overwrites the association. Adversarial input, no peer failure/restart.

title: [Bugs] AMF NGAP worker permanently lost after handler panic, no restart mechanism
pass1_rationale: A panicking NGAP worker is never restarted while its queue keeps accepting messages, which silently vanish.
pass2_rationale: AMF NGAP worker goroutines die permanently after handler panics triggered by a malicious Handover nil-deref PoC, eventually blocking NGSetup; adversarial-input/fuzzing trigger and internal worker-pool robustness, no NF/peer failure event.

title: Bug: PDU Session Establishment fails after AMF pod restart due to stale CommunicationClient
pass1_rationale: After an AMF pod restart the SMF keeps a stale CommunicationClient; N1N2MessageTransfer hangs for all UEs until SMF restart.
pass2_rationale: After AMF pod restart with a new IP, SMF keeps a cached per-SMContext CommunicationClient and NRF/cache return stale AMF profiles, so N1N2MessageTransfer times out to the dead pod IP and PDU session establishment fails for all UEs (T3580 x5) until SMF restart.

title: UE IP allocation walks outside the configured pool after SMF restarts (SMF_COUNT stride is unbounded)
pass1_rationale: IP allocator strides by a restart counter persisted in MongoDB; after restarts it silently hands out addresses outside the routed pool.
pass2_rationale: On every SMF restart a DB-persisted monotonic smfCount is incremented and used as a 5000-address stride, so after one restart (on a /24) SMF hands out UE IPs outside the configured pool; session comes up and uplink works but downlink is dead. Restart-count misused as instance index with no pool bound check (other); silent, and a ping probe would show persistent data-plane loss.

title: After restarting sgw the UE cann't attah again
pass1_rationale: After an SGW restart the MME keeps using TEIDs the SGW no longer knows; the UE cannot attach again.
pass2_rationale: After SGW restart the MME keeps old session state and sends Create Session with TEID unknown to SGW (SGW logs ASSERT !(sgw_ue)), so the UE cannot re-attach; thread: maintainer says SGW/PGW restart not supported. Process keeps running (repeated assert logs).

title: After restarting sgw the UE cann't attah again

title: MME Restarts if SGs Interface is Down
pass1_rationale: With the SGs peer unreachable the MME restarts whenever a UE attaches.
pass2_rationale: The MME restarts when a UE connects while the configured SGs (VLR) peer is unreachable. The peer is the MSC/VLR, which is outside the listed core NFs, and there is no clear cross-NF state issue. Thread: maintainer calls this expected behavior with no fix.

title: Stray PFCP associations - SGWC and SMF
pass1_rationale: Unlisted UPF associated; configuration.
pass2_rationale: Thread: after one of two UPFs is killed and SMF enters association retry, SMF round-robin still assigns new sessions to the dead UPF because selection does not check that the PFCP association is still active; failures are logged and a retry lands on the live UPF, so not persistent.

title: NRF closes HTTP socket if any unregistered NF sends Heartbeat and then Registration request
pass1_rationale: After an NRF restart (empty cache) a heartbeat from a still-running NF makes the NRF close the socket and later crash.
pass2_rationale: After NRF restart the third-party NF gets 404 on heartbeat and re-registers, and NRF asserts/crashes; thread: root cause was a generic bug receiving large HTTP/2 messages, so it is unclear whether the failure is restart-specific or would hit any large registration.

title: SA attach issue
pass1_rationale: SA attach issue; configuration.
pass2_rationale: After all CP NFs restart while the UPF keeps running, the SMF re-associates over PFCP but UE attach fails repeatedly: the UPF returns session-context errors and the CP stalls. Thread: maintainer reproduced it by restarting all NFs except the UPF, fixed it in main, and the reporter confirmed. Labelled stale-restoration because pre-restart UPF state conflicts after re-association; the exact mechanism is not stated.

title: NRF assert
pass1_rationale: NRF assert; insufficient information.
pass2_rationale: NRF heartbeat timers expired for all NFs (No heartbeat, NF de-registered) and the ensuing burst of NF re-registration PUTs (plus PFCP re-association) crashed NRF with nrf_event_new assertion (event pool); thread: maintainer says fixed in v2.2.4.

title: Sequence Of Start And Config Reload
pass1_rationale: Start order question.
pass2_rationale: Mostly startup-order/config questions; one sub-issue: when a UPF (UPF-initiated association) is shut down, SMF does not select the remaining associated UPF and loops ('No UPFs are PFCP associated that are suited to RR'). Maintainer fixed RR selection, but the error also appeared with both UPFs up and the final fix was a config change, so restart-relatedness is unclear.

title: SMF Fatal Error v2.2.9 - Invalid Downlink Data Service Information
pass1_rationale: After the SMF crashes and restarts, all NFs must be restarted to become operative again.
pass2_rationale: SMF fatal error (Invalid Downlink Data Service Information) when a UE reconnects after UE context release; normal-path crash fixed in v2.3.0, not triggered by an NF/peer failure (the SMF restart afterwards is a consequence).

title: SGWC crashes randomly after disconnecting a VoLTE call
pass1_rationale: SGW-C crash after VoLTE call; no NF failure.
pass2_rationale: Thread: eNB sends GTP-U Error Indication during Delete Bearer procedure; the resulting DDN makes MME overwrite bearer->xact, so the Delete Bearer Response carries a wrong sequence number and SGW-C crashes. Root cause is a transaction-context overwrite on Error Indication handling (other).

title: MME crash and restart
pass1_rationale: MME crashes and is restarted by systemd; sessions stale afterwards; crash cause unknown.
pass2_rationale: Main bug: a normal-path MME crash (pkbuf/asn1c memory with large UERadioCapability). Thread: after each MME crash/restart, sessions pile up in SGW-U/UPF (715 vs about 30 at SGW-C/SMF). The maintainer confirmed PFCP has no IMSI, so duplicates cannot be reconciled after an MME (or SMF) restart. Orphan state found only by inspecting counters.

title: Segmentation fault after deregister an NF
pass1_rationale: NRF segfault on NF deregistration (explicit API call, no failure).
pass2_rationale: NRF segfaults when an NF (AUSF) that has a subscription for its type is de-registered via DELETE nf-instance; concerns NRF registration/subscription state on NF departure, but it is a graceful deregistration rather than a crash/heartbeat-loss, so the failure-event criterion is ambiguous.

title: Cannot receive SBI message
pass1_rationale: Redeployment problem; configuration.
pass2_rationale: After switching Amarisoft/Open5GS from SA to NSA/4G and back to SA, UE cannot be found and AMF gets SBI 504 errors; maintainer says some NF did not respond but thread unresolved, so failure event and bug-vs-config are unclear.

title: NG RESET ACKNOWLEDGE error
pass1_rationale: NG Reset Acknowledge apparently not sent; protocol handling question.
pass2_rationale: AMF fails to actually send NG Reset Acknowledge when the RAN node sends a (partial) NG Reset, so the reset procedure with the gNB never completes; maintainer fixed it. Visible as missing ack at the RAN/pcap; no evidence of persistent UE service failure.

title: feedback requested: PFCP synchronization?
pass1_rationale: UPF restart loses all PFCP state while SMF/SGW-C keep sessions; attached UEs have no traffic until the CP is restarted.
pass2_rationale: When the UP side (SGW-U/UPF) crashes and restarts it loses all PFCP state, but SGW-C/SMF keep the old sessions. Already-attached UEs cannot send traffic and disconnects fail, and the whole CP has to be restarted to resync. The data-plane outage is persistent and visible to a UE probe.

title: SMFs in different containers: no heartbeat error after try to discover udm
pass1_rationale: Multi-container configuration problem.
pass2_rationale: Second SMF in another container logs 'No heartbeat' from NRF after UDM discovery, then keeps de-/re-registering with NRF (inconsistent SMF/NRF state). Heartbeat loss is present but the thread is a 'what am I misconfiguring' question with no resolution; code bug vs config unclear.

title: SMF Number Of Sessions Not Updating After UEs Have Been Deleted
pass1_rationale: After the gNB and UEs are removed the AMF reflects reality but the SMF keeps the sessions active.
pass2_rationale: SMF session count stays after gNB/UEs removed; thread: maintainer says UE contexts are intentionally kept (like idle) on gNB loss, and the bug actually fixed was a BSF binding keyed on S-NSSAI+DNN breaking normal deregistration of a 2nd UE (normal path).

title: About the SGW-U down in the CUPS environment hundreds of kilometers away
pass1_rationale: Pool allocation failure after 5 days; no restart trigger.
pass2_rationale: SGW-U crashes with ogs_pool_alloc() failed (timer pool) and xact assert 15 s after heartbeat loss/de-association from a distant SGW-C after 5 days uptime; no replies, so unclear whether it is a re-association leak bug or resource sizing (reporter asks for parameters).

title: New crash lockups since 2.4.11
pass1_rationale: Spoofing log lockups.
pass2_rationale: UPF drops uplink as Source IP Spoofing (TEID/UE IP mismatch between UEs) after ~48h until services restart; thread: maintainer first blamed an SMF restart (TEID mismatch SGW-U/UPF) then found no SMF restart and fixed SGW-U sessions not deleted properly, and v2.5.0 still failed, so the failure-event link is ambiguous.

title: UPF and SMF crash
pass1_rationale: UPF crash followed by SMF crash; causality unclear.
pass2_rationale: UPF and SMF crash on start in Kubernetes on Alpine; thread: stack overflow on musl/Alpine, fixed. Normal-path platform crash, not a restart/peer-failure bug.

title: [AMF] NG_Reset in response for UE_Context_Release_Command causes a fatal error (crash)
pass1_rationale: An NG Reset received in response to UE Context Release Command crashes the AMF.
pass2_rationale: gNB sends NG Reset (peer lost-state signal) in response to a UE Context Release Command; AMF's handling of the reset against the pending UE context release hits a fatal error and the AMF crashes. Fixed in main per maintainer.

title: [Bug]: [SMF]  smf_npcf_smpolicycontrol_build_delete: Assertion sess->sm_context_ref failed
pass1_rationale: Shutting down the host running the UPFs/SGWs makes the SMF crash (assertion on sm_context_ref) instead of failing sessions.
pass2_rationale: Shutting down the host running UPFs causes PFCP heartbeat loss; SMF's N4 no-heartbeat cleanup loop (reused 'next' iterator and already-freed node pointer, session without sm_context_ref) hits an assertion and SMF crashes. Thread: maintainer fixed both issues.

title: ogs_sbi_client_handler() failed [-1] (../lib/sbi/path.c:62)
pass1_rationale: Restarting a single service triggers 500 errors in peer NFs; insufficient detail.
pass2_rationale: NF registration via SCP to NRF gets 500 response_handler() failed; happens even on fresh start of NRF with SCP (comment), no restart-specific behaviour and no resolution; likely setup/usage issue.

title: [Bug]: Incomplete NF Instance Cleanup Due to Reference Counting Error Causes Fallback to Default Port 80 After UDR Restart
pass1_rationale: After a UDR restart the UDM keeps a stale NF-instance/client (refcount error) and falls back to port 80; registrations fail.
pass2_rationale: After a UDR restart, the UDM still holds the released UDR nf_instance pointer in service_type_array (incomplete cleanup / reference count). It uses that client's default port 80, and UE re-registration fails with connection refused. Thread: maintainer fixed it by storing nf_instance_id and checking validity on recovery.

title: [Bug]: AMF crash in common_register_state due to stale ran_ue_id after Handoverrequired and duplicate IMSI registration
pass1_rationale: Handover/duplicate registration race; no NF failure.
pass2_rationale: AMF assert(ran_ue) crash from stale ran_ue_id after an incomplete handover plus duplicate-IMSI registration, triggered when the Process-one gNBs are 'released'; unclear whether this gNB release is a peer failure/disconnect or the bug is just a handover/duplicate-IMSI path.

title: [Bug]: AMF fails to handle GOAWAY frames and reuses a closed tcp stream
pass1_rationale: After a UDM GOAWAY the AMF keeps reusing the closed HTTP/2 connection and subsequent requests fail.
pass2_rationale: AMF reportedly reuses a TCP connection after UDM GOAWAY caused by a short idle timeout. Not a peer restart/failure, and the maintainer could not reproduce it (curl opens a new connection). Closed for inactivity.

title: gtpu TEID Issue - EPC Fail over recovery
pass1_rationale: After the main EPC restarts and the eNB fails back, the UE re-attaches but its user-plane traffic is dropped.
pass2_rationale: Dual-EPC failover: after main EPC is brought back up and eNB re-connects, UE re-attaches but ping fails (user plane broken); restart event is clear but no replies/root cause, so unclear whether an Open5GS state bug, eNB-side stale state, or deployment misconfiguration.

title: AMF aborts before sending NRF subscriptions (v2.7.5)
pass1_rationale: AMF abort at startup.
pass2_rationale: AMF loses NRF heartbeat and repeatedly re-registers; thread: each re-registration cycle created duplicate NF-status subscriptions and stale subscription_data was not cleaned on non-204 DELETE, exhausting the pool until AMF asserts in ogs_sbi_subscription_data_add. Crash is visible, but it took hours of re-registration cycles, so a short test would not see it.

title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)
pass1_rationale: After gNB SCTP reconnection AMF/SMF keep stale UE context; N1N2 transfers fail with HTTP 400 and the UE stays registered without data.
pass2_rationale: After gNB SCTP drop and reconnect, re-registering UEs get stale AMF/SMF state (thread: hypothesised zombie sess_list transplanted on SUCI re-attach; SMF did not release session on N1N2 400), so PDU session establishment fails every ~16 s with HTTP 400 and IPs leak; only restarting AMF/SMF recovers.

title: [Bug]: GTP-U Error Indication on S5-U tears down the whole IMS PDN without notifying the MME (VoLTE UE stuck until re-attach)
pass1_rationale: On a GTP-U Error Indication the SGW/PGW locally deletes the IMS PDN without notifying the MME; UE stuck until re-attach.
pass2_rationale: On a GTP-U Error Indication (peer lost state) the SMF/PGW-C deletes the whole IMS PDN locally without Delete Bearer Request, so MME/UE keep a ghost PDN and the UE cannot make VoLTE calls until re-attach; SMF logs ERROR at the time, and IMS service stays down.

title: [Bug]: SGW-C leaves an empty session after default bearer deletion failure
pass1_rationale: Default bearer deletion failure response; no NF failure.
pass2_rationale: Starts from an Error Indication for the IMS default bearer (a peer lost-state signal), followed by Delete Bearer Request and a Cause-only failure response from the MME. SGW-C removes only the default bearer and leaves an empty sgwc_sess_t; a later Release Access Bearers Request hits ogs_assert and aborts SGW-C.

title: NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF session, blackholing the UE
pass1_rationale: UE re-registration while NG context is held; no NF failure.
pass2_rationale: After gNB restart forces re-registration while AMF holds the NG context, t_ng_holding expiry removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF/UPF session, so DL FAR keeps pointing at a dead gNB TEID and the UE is blackholed with no paging and no error; reporter says it persists until the UE re-registers (getting a new IP since the old session still holds it).

title: [Bug]: Repeated GTP-U Error Indications can crash SMF during EPC bearer deactivation
pass1_rationale: Two Error Indication reports for one bearer start two deactivation procedures and crash the SMF.
pass2_rationale: Repeated GTP-U Error Indications (peer reports lost state) for the same EPC bearer each start a separate deactivation. With no SGW-C responses, the duplicate PFCP remove makes the SMF hit ogs_assert(bearer) and abort. The bearer state tied to the peer event is mis-released: double removal, and the default bearer is removed leaving an empty session.

title: UDM: SDM subscriptions are never released for UEs that vanish without deregistering, so the 4096 pool fills and registrations fail as "5GS services not allowed" with no AMF-side error
pass1_rationale: UDM SDM subscriptions are never released for UEs that vanish without deregistering; failed party is the UE, not an NF.
pass2_rationale: Killing the RAN simulator (SCTP drop) makes AMF send a burst of SM-context updates; thread: reporter's debug rerun shows SBI failures abort release for ~30% of UEs, so UE contexts and UDM SDM subscriptions are never released and the 4096 pool fills over repeated kills, rejecting registrations. AMF logs ERRORs at gNB loss (thread), and exhaustion needs many cycles/hundreds of UEs; not reproduced on 2.8.0.

title: SBI client never recovers from a half-dead HTTP/2 connection (requests keep timing out forever)
pass1_rationale: After the peer stops answering on an established HTTP/2 connection the SBI client keeps reusing it; requests time out forever.
pass2_rationale: After request overload, the SMF stops answering on the established HTTP/2 connection; AMF SBI client (libcurl multiplexing) never tears down the half-dead connection, so every AMF->SMF request times out until process restart and PDU sessions fail. Killing the connection restores service immediately.

title: [Bug]: SMF aborts on PFCP Session Deletion timeout when the associated SBI stream is gone (sess_5gc_timeout: Assertion 'stream' failed)
pass1_rationale: SMF aborts on PFCP Session Deletion timeout; on restart it loses UE IP allocations, causing duplicate IPs and broken downlink.
pass2_rationale: When the UPF does not answer a PFCP Session Deletion Request (peer unresponsive) and the AMF-side SBI stream is already gone, sess_5gc_timeout hits ogs_assert(stream) and aborts the SMF. The restarted SMF has lost its UE IP allocations, giving duplicate IPs and crash loops under churn. Root cause is an unguarded NULL on the peer-timeout path (other).

title: [Bug]: SMF: not releasing existing UE sessions after UPF failure (Heartbeat timeout)
pass1_rationale: SMF never releases UE sessions after the only UPF is declared failed via heartbeat timeout.
pass2_rationale: After UPF heartbeat timeout the SMF never releases existing sessions (4G path; thread: 5G released only via reselect_upf), keeping them active and accounting while the UPF is gone until it returns and restoration runs; heartbeat give-up is logged and the UE outage is inherent to the UPF being down, so a crash/persistent-failure oracle would not flag it.

title: AMF: SMF discovery failure in PDU session establishment may accumulate AMF PDU session contexts  #1
pass1_rationale: When SMF selection fails the AMF keeps the PDU session context it registered; contexts accumulate.
pass2_rationale: While the SMF is down or undiscoverable, the AMF registers a PDU session context, SMF selection fails, and the context is never removed. These survivors persist (copied on re-registration) and cost a 1 s timeout each on the single N1 thread at deregistration. The orphan state itself is not reported, and service recovers once the SMF is back.

title: AMF: N1N2MessageSubscribe response timeout may orphan stored subscriptions
pass1_rationale: Internal timeout orphans a subscription; no NF failure.
pass2_rationale: N1N2MessageSubscribe stored after the HTTP thread times out (1 s), so subscriptions are orphaned; trigger is an APP-task stall that the PoC induces via an unresponsive NSSF (peer unreachability) but the reporter says any CPU/scheduling stall suffices, so it is mainly a timeout race rather than clearly a peer-failure bug.

title: UPF keeps the PFCP sessions of an association when the same CP function sets it up again
pass1_rationale: Association re-setup by the same CP function overwrites the association but keeps the old PFCP sessions, TEIDs and UE IPs.
pass2_rationale: After SMF restart and re-association the UPF overwrites the association but keeps all old PFCP sessions; the restarted SMF reuses CP SEIDs from 1, so new sessions collide with kept ones and are rejected (UE gets PDU Session Establishment Reject #38) and the orphaned sessions are never deleted.
